creditBankEquityShareOfDeposits.citation: Median of cushion plus other assets less deposits, as a share of deposits, over the 3,194 FDIC-insured banks under $1 billion, June 30, 2026 call reports (data/tables/town-bank-shapes.json).

spread.citation: 10th and 90th percentiles of the same banks.

creditLineMonthsOfPayroll.citation: Small firms seek lines covering a few months of operating costs (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey, 2023 Report on Employer Firms).

spread.citation: Small firms seek lines covering a few months of operating costs (Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey, 2023 Report on Employer Firms).

creditPrimeSpreadPct.citation: Small business lines price at prime plus one to three points (Federal Reserve Survey of Terms of Business Lending, 2010-2017; SBA 7(a) maximums).

spread.citation: Small business lines price at prime plus one to three points (Federal Reserve Survey of Terms of Business Lending, 2010-2017; SBA 7(a) maximums).

creditRiskSpreadPct.citation: A borrower whose sales barely cover its wages pays more (SBA 7(a) spread caps by loan size).

spread.unit: percentage points at the weakest record
spread.citation: A borrower whose sales barely cover its wages pays more (SBA 7(a) spread caps by loan size).

creditCapitalAppetiteSlope.citation: A bank lends less as its capital falls below where it opened, on a sliding scale (Federal Reserve Senior Loan Officer Survey: tightening with capital and risk).

spread.citation: A bank lends less as its capital falls below where it opened, on a sliding scale (Federal Reserve Senior Loan Officer Survey: tightening with capital and risk).

creditMaxLimitsPerEquity.citation: Small banks hold loans of about eight to twelve times their equity (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, community banks).

spread.unit: line limits per dollar of equity
spread.citation: Small banks hold loans of about eight to twelve times their equity (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, community banks).

creditDepositsInThousands.citation: FDIC Summary of Deposits reports deposits in thousands of dollars.

creditPersonalSpreadPct.citation: Commercial bank 24-month personal loan rates ran about 6 to 9 points over prime, 2015-2024 (Federal Reserve G.19, terms of credit).

spread.citation: Commercial bank 24-month personal loan rates ran about 6 to 9 points over prime, 2015-2024 (Federal Reserve G.19, terms of credit).

creditPersonalTermMonths.citation: Federal Reserve G.19 reports personal loans at a 24-month term.

creditDtiReferencePct.citation: 12 CFR 1026.43(e)(2)(vi) (2014-2021 general qualified mortgage): total debt payments at most 43 percent of monthly income.

creditDtiSlope.citation: A lender's yes falls smoothly as payments approach and pass the reference share of income.

spread.citation: A lender's yes falls smoothly as payments approach and pass the reference share of income.

creditChargeOffDays.citation: FFIEC Uniform Retail Credit Classification and Account Management Policy (65 FR 36903, 2000): closed-end retail loans are charged off at 120 days past due.

creditBorrowNeedWeight.citation: A household with few days of money left wants to borrow.

spread.citation: A household with few days of money left wants to borrow.

creditBorrowCostWeight.citation: The payment against income weighs against borrowing.

spread.unit: score per share of monthly income
spread.citation: The payment against income weighs against borrowing.

creditBorrowBaseline.citation: How far borrowing sits below doing without, before need; checked against G.19 consumer credit growth and SCF borrowing shares.

spread.citation: How far borrowing sits below doing without, before need; checked against G.19 consumer credit growth and SCF borrowing shares.

creditPersonalMonthsOfCosts.citation: Personal loans cover a few months of costs (SCF 2022 median unsecured installment balance about 2 to 3 months of median household spending).

spread.citation: Personal loans cover a few months of costs (SCF 2022 median unsecured installment balance about 2 to 3 months of median household spending).

creditHouseholdMonthlyLendingShare.citation: Consumer loans are about 5 to 8 percent of community bank assets (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, 2019-2024), turning over in about two years; new household lending per month is a small share of the bank's funds. A first generated-world month without this cap lent all of the town bank's cash to 993 households.

spread.unit: share of the bank's cash per month
spread.citation: FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, community banks.

creditReportYears.citation: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681c(a)(4): accounts charged to profit and loss may be reported for seven years.

creditChargedOffYesShare.citation: A lender's yes to a household with a charge-off on its report is a small share of its yes otherwise; a charge-off is among the most damaging items on a credit report.

spread.citation: A lender's yes to a household with a charge-off on its report is a small share of its yes otherwise; a charge-off is among the most damaging items on a credit report.

creditMinimumLoanMinor.citation: FDIC 2011 Survey of Banks' Efforts to Serve the Unbanked and Underbanked, other products (https://www.fdic.gov/consumer-research/2011-bank-survey-results-other-products): of banks offering unsecured personal loans, 43% set no minimum and another 53% a minimum of $2,500 or less.

spread.citation: FDIC 2011 Survey of Banks' Efforts to Serve the Unbanked and Underbanked, other products (https://www.fdic.gov/consumer-research/2011-bank-survey-results-other-products): of banks offering unsecured personal loans, 43% set no minimum and another 53% a minimum of $2,500 or less.

creditResidentsCashMonths.citation: Households keep about a month of income in cash and checking to spend, the rest in savings (Federal Reserve SCF 2022 transaction-account balances; JPMorgan Chase Institute checking-balance studies).

spread.citation: Households keep about a month of income in cash and checking to spend, the rest in savings (Federal Reserve SCF 2022 transaction-account balances; JPMorgan Chase Institute checking-balance studies).

creditDepositRatePassThrough.citation: Banks pass a small share of the policy rate to savings deposits (FDIC national deposit rates against the federal funds rate, 2015-2024: savings near 0.45% at a 5.3% funds rate).

spread.citation: Banks pass a small share of the policy rate to savings deposits (FDIC national deposit rates against the federal funds rate, 2015-2024: savings near 0.45% at a 5.3% funds rate).

creditDepositRateFloor.citation: The lowest savings rate banks paid when the policy rate sat at zero (FDIC national savings rate, 2021: about 0.05%).

spread.citation: The lowest savings rate banks paid when the policy rate sat at zero (FDIC national savings rate, 2021: about 0.05%).

creditBankReserveShare.citation: Community banks' cash and balances due from other banks against deposits (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, community banks, 2019-2024).

spread.citation: Community banks' cash and balances due from other banks against deposits (FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile, community banks, 2019-2024).

creditStartupEquityShare.citation: SBA SOP 50 10 8 (effective June 1, 2025): a startup borrower injects equity of at least 10 percent of total project cost; the loan covers at most the rest.

creditStartupDebtServiceCoverage.citation: SBA SOP 50 10 7.1 and 50 10 8: a 7(a) loan to a new business needs projected cash flow of at least 1.15 times its debt service.

creditHomeEquityCombinedLoanToValue.citation: Home equity lines lend up to 80 to 90 percent of a home's value less what is owed on it (CFPB, What you should know about home equity lines of credit, 2021).

spread.unit: share of home value, all liens
spread.citation: CFPB, What you should know about home equity lines of credit (2021): lenders typically limit combined borrowing to 80 to 90 percent of the home's value.

creditHomeEquityMarginPct.citation: A home equity line's rate is the prime rate plus a margin, commonly zero to two points (CFPB, What you should know about home equity lines of credit, 2021; Federal Reserve G.19 notes HELOCs are variable-rate loans indexed to prime).

spread.citation: CFPB, What you should know about home equity lines of credit (2021): the rate is an index, usually prime, plus a margin set by the lender.

creditHomeEquityTermYears.citation: A home equity line draws for about 10 years and repays over the next 10 to 20 (CFPB, What you should know about home equity lines of credit, 2021); repaid here as level payments from the start.

spread.citation: CFPB (2021): draw periods of about 10 years, repayment periods of 10 to 20 years.
